Across several interactions, my symptoms were dismissed or minimised without proper assessment. Concerns were not investigated thoroughly, and clinical curiosity was replaced with reassurance that was unsupported by evidence. When action was required, the default response was delay.

There has been persistent inconsistency. Different clinicians have given different answers to the same issues, with thresholds and explanations changing depending on who I spoke to. This creates confusion, undermines confidence, and suggests a lack of coherent clinical decision-making within the practice.

Follow-up has been weak. I have repeatedly had to chase appointments, prescriptions, or next steps, rather than these being managed proactively. Progress only seems to occur after escalation, which indicates a reactive approach to care rather than a responsible or preventative one.

Responsibility is often deflected to “policy,” “guidelines,” or system limitations, rather than clinicians owning decisions and explaining them clearly. This leaves the patient carrying the burden of navigating problems that should be handled within primary care.

The cumulative effect is a loss of trust. I now approach interactions expecting resistance rather than support, which is not how a patient–GP relationship should function. At no point should a patient feel they must fight repeatedly to receive basic, consistent medical care.

In summary, this practice has managed risk for itself rather than prioritising patient outcomes. The repeated delays, dismissals, and inconsistencies fall below what I would reasonably expect from competent primary care. Based on my experiences, I cannot recommend this practice.

Nothing more then another group of people lining thier own pockets and no regard for consumers health or condition management

don't know why there are so many bad reviews about this place. Yes it can be quiet difficult at times to get an appointment but that isn't there fault. There's only so many appointments and time in the day. My only gripe with appointments is it's ring on the day. But there are always elderly patience waiting outside the surgery before half past 8 wanting appointments. In my own experience I have always managed to ring and get to see DR Lowe whenever needed. And Dr Lowe is hands down the best doctor I have ever dealt with. After years of struggling with my mental health and not knowing what's wrong with me or why I am like I am and using other doctors and nurses and getting absolutely nowhere I went to see DR Lowe, who was so understanding and could see how much I was struggling, he has helped me so much through many dark times. He got me reffered to a psychiatrist very quickly where after years of struggle was diagnosed with Bipolar. If it wasn't for Dr Lowe this would never have happened.
